decisions.reason: As a core airfield-control product with a strongly public launch claim and clear fit to the firm's automation strategy, management is likely to stay committed and view any weaker uptake as temporary.
The surveillance display extends the established airport-operations portfolio and supports integrated tower and airfield solutions, so prior development effort and strategic fit favor persistence.
The training program is closely tied to the firm's installed systems and service model, and because it complements the core offer management would likely retain it rather than signal retreat.
This narrower training course appears less central and less visibly committed than the firm's system products, so it is the easiest offering to withdraw or absorb into broader training services.

Collaboration software sits at the heart of the firm's stated move toward real-time information sharing and collaborative decision-making, which makes management especially prone to continue backing it.

The multilateration surveillance system likely required substantial R&D and was publicly announced as an advanced flagship solution, so escalation of commitment strongly favors keeping it on the market.
